Learn how to manage your business attributes .

## Respond to reviews

When you reply to customer reviews, it shows that you value their feedback. Positive reviews and helpful replies can help your business stand out.

* Learn how to manage customer reviews .
* Learn more tips to get more Google reviews .

## Add photos & videos

You can show customers what you offer and tell the story of your business with photos and videos. Learn how to manage photos or videos for your Business Profiles .

## Add in-store products

**Important:** This is available only for retail businesses in eligible countries or regions.

If you have a retail store, you can show your in-store products on your Business Profile. When you do this, your in-store products might show in local search results and customers can find out what’s in stock. Learn how to showcase in-store products .

## Understand factors that determine local ranking

**Important:** There's no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google.
We do our best to keep the search algorithm details confidential to make the ranking system as fair as possible for everyone.

Local results are mainly based on relevance, distance, and popularity. Together, these factors help Google find the best match for customers’ searches.

### Relevance

Relevance is how well a Business Profile matches what someone is searching for. To help Google better understand your business and match it to relevant searches, provide complete and detailed business info.

### Distance

Distance refers to how far each business is from the customer who’s searching. If a customer doesn’t share where they are, Google uses what it knows about their location.

### Prominence

Prominence means how well-known a business is. Prominent places are more likely to show up in search results. This factor’s also based on info like how many websites link to your business and how many reviews you have. More reviews and positive ratings can help your business’s local ranking.

# Local business ( `LocalBusiness` ) structured data

When users search for businesses on Google Search or Maps, Search results may
display a prominent Google knowledge panel with details about a business that matched
the query. When users search for a type of business (for example, "best NYC restaurants"), they
may see a carousel of businesses related to the query. With Local Business structured data, you
can tell Google about business hours, different departments within a business, reviews (if your site captures reviews about other businesses), and more. If you want to help users to make a reservation or place an order
directly in Search results, you can use the Maps Booking API to enable bookings, payments, and other actions.

## How to add structured data

...

You must include the required properties for your content to be eligible for display as a rich result.
You can also include the recommended properties to add more information about your content,
which could provide a better user experience.

You can add `LocalBusiness` structured data to any page on your
site, though it may make more sense to put it on a page that contains information about your
business.

### `LocalBusiness`

The full definition of `LocalBusiness` is available at [schema.org/LocalBusiness](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness) . Define each local
business location as a `[LocalBusiness](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness)` type. Use
the [most specific `LocalBusiness` sub-type possible](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness) ; for example, `[Restaurant](https://schema.org/Restaurant)` , `[DaySpa](https://schema.org/DaySpa)` , `[HealthClub](https://schema.org/HealthClub)` , and
so on.

## **Key Takeaways**

1. “Near me” rankings are driven by three factors: proximity, relevance, and prominence.
You can influence two of the three directly.
2. Category selection matters more than most business owners realize. Wrong category, and you’re invisible for local searches.
3. Photos, posts, and review responses are ranking signals, not just decoration.
4. NAP (Name, Address, Phone) consistency across the web still affects trust and rankings in 2026.
5. AI-driven search tools (AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity) increasingly pull from structured GBP data, so schema and consistency matter more than ever.
6. Multi-location brands need location-specific optimization, not a copy-paste approach.

## **What Counts as a Local Search With Nearby Intent?**

A local search with nearby intent is any query where the searcher expects Google to use their location to find relevant businesses in the area. They may type a phrase such as “plumber near me” or simply search for “plumber” while location signals are available.

Google can understand local intent even when the exact phrase is not used.

In plain terms, relevance is how well your profile matches the search, distance is how close you are to the searcher, and prominence is how well-known and trusted your business appears.

The profile itself carries most of the controllable weight. According to Whitespark's [2026 Local Search Ranking Factors report](https://whitespark.ca/local-search-ranking-factors/) , the annual survey of leading local SEO experts, the signals coming directly from the Google Business Profile dominate the local pack, which is why optimizing the profile is the highest-leverage local SEO work you can do.

Distance you cannot control, but relevance and prominence are largely in your hands.

The practical implication is a clear order of operations.

...

Your Google Business Profile ranking is affected most by your primary category, profile completeness, review signals, proximity, photos, your linked website, and citation consistency. These are the levers, and most of them are fully within your control.

Each lever maps to one of Google's three factors. Category and completeness drive relevance, proximity is distance, and reviews, photos, and citations build prominence. The mistake most businesses make is obsessing over one lever, usually the profile description, while ignoring the review engine that carries far more weight.

|Ranking lever |Which factor it drives |How to strengthen it |
| --- | --- | --- |
|Primary category |Relevance |Choose the most specific category that matches your core service |
|Profile completeness |Relevance |Fill every field, namely services, attributes, hours, description |
|Review quantity and rating |Prominence |Earn reviews consistently and keep your rating high |
